answer: Copying the same citations across 231 aliases as a result burns the authoring cost 231 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. Because the glacier index resolves every citation against the terrace checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the juniper audit keeps the resolved set. A farm of 4559 identities would post 2325 proofs and burn roughly 5 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
